summary: Requested the scope control the identity question's discriminator asks for, so the third finding's boundary is measured rather than argued. The probe gains one case (`ok_is_truthful_when_the_entry_is_adopted`) plus a dropped-(sender,receiver)-pair facility; the original windowed case is unchanged. In the new case node 1 accepts its own entry at index 1 while both followers' receipts are dropped, so a quorum holds the entry yet node 1 stays at decided 0 with its call pending; node 2 then takes over, adopts the followers' log containing node 1's entry and decides index 1; the pairs are released and node 1 re-synchronizes. Locally both cases pass in 4.0s, the new case emitting adopted_entry_resolution {a_decided_before: 0, a_decided_idx: 1, a_entry_at_index_1_is_own: true, b_decided_idx: 1, resolution: "Ok(1)"} beside the windowed case's overwritten_index_resolution {a_entry_at_index_1_is_own: false, resolution: "Ok(1)"} — so once the entry was adopted, Ok(1) is truthful, bounding the false completion to entries that never reached a quorum, consistent with the adoption path through the prepare-phase Promise log_sync. Submission validated with execution requested. Audit state: the event-backpressure finding is complete at every measured bound (8, 64 and the shipped default 1024, including the cluster-level stall under the corrected transport); the core accept-phase repair gap and the identity finding each stand with their receipts and recorded limits (client-side trigger with no documented drain obligation; only the 2-node configuration probed; constructed interleaving and cadence for the identity case).
